questions.q: CSV files land in an S3 bucket under `raw/`. Three independent consumers (a Lambda function, a Step Functions workflow and a bus in another account) must react only to non-empty `.csv` objects. Which design needs the least custom code?

options.t: Turn on "Send notifications to Amazon EventBridge" for the bucket and create a rule with prefix, suffix and `numeric` size filters and three targets
options.why: Right: EventBridge patterns filter on key prefix, suffix and size, and one rule can have up to 5 targets, including another account's bus.

options.t: One S3 Event Notification with prefix `raw/` and suffix `.csv` to the Lambda function, which then calls the other two
options.why: Wrong: S3 notifications cannot filter on size, allow one destination per config, and the Lambda becomes glue code.

options.t: Three S3 Event Notifications with the same prefix, one per consumer
options.why: Wrong: overlapping prefixes for the same event type are rejected, and Step Functions and buses are not notification destinations.

options.t: A scheduled Lambda that lists the bucket every minute
options.why: Wrong: polling adds delay, code and request cost.

questions.explain: S3 → EventBridge gives full content filters and several targets per rule.
questions.remember: Several consumers, size or wildcard filters, or Step Functions/cross-account targets on S3 events → S3 to EventBridge plus a rule. Simplest single S3 → Lambda/SQS path → plain S3 Event Notification.
variants: Only one Lambda consumer and a prefix filter → a plain S3 Event Notification is enough.
Must skip zero-byte "folder" objects → add `detail.object.size` `numeric > 0` in the pattern.

questions.q: A team created an EventBridge rule on the default bus for `source=aws.s3`, `detail-type=Object Created` on bucket `landing`, in the bucket's Region. Uploads succeed but the rule never fires and `MatchedEvents` shows nothing. What is the most likely cause?

options.t: The rule needs state `ENABLED_WITH_ALL_CLOUDTRAIL_MANAGEMENT_EVENTS`
options.why: Wrong: that state is for read-only CloudTrail management events, not native S3 EventBridge events.

options.t: S3 event delivery to EventBridge was never turned on for the bucket
options.why: Right: S3 → EventBridge is off by default and must be switched on per bucket.

options.t: S3 events are delivered only to custom buses
options.why: Wrong: AWS service events go only to the default bus.

options.t: The rule needs a CloudTrail trail with S3 data events
options.why: Wrong: that is only for CloudTrail-based API-call events; native S3 events need the bucket switch.

questions.explain: S3 → EventBridge is a per-bucket switch, off by default.
questions.remember: No S3 events in EventBridge → check the bucket's "Send notifications to Amazon EventBridge" setting, the Region, and that the rule is on the default bus.
variants: Rule lives on a custom bus → add a forwarding rule on the default bus to that custom bus.
Rule fires for 0-byte keys ending in `/` → filter `size > 0` or `anything-but` suffix `/`.

questions.q: A new object in S3 must start a single AWS Glue ETL job. A developer tries to add the Glue job as a target of an EventBridge rule and cannot find it. Which TWO designs work? (Choose 2.)

options.t: Rule target = a Glue workflow whose EVENT trigger starts the job
options.why: Right: Glue workflows are rule targets (the role needs `glue:notifyEvent`).

options.t: Rule target = SQS FIFO queue that Glue polls automatically
options.why: Wrong: Glue jobs do not poll SQS queues.

options.t: Rule target = a Step Functions state machine that runs Glue `startJobRun.sync`
options.why: Right: Step Functions is a rule target and can start the job and wait for it.

options.t: Rule target = the Glue Data Catalog table
options.why: Wrong: a catalog table is not a target and cannot run a job.

questions.explain: A Glue job is not a direct rule target; a Glue workflow or Step Functions is.
questions.remember: Event must start a Glue job → rule → Glue workflow (EVENT trigger) or Step Functions; time-based start of one job → Scheduler universal target `glue:startJobRun`.
variants: Many small files should start one Glue run → Glue workflow EVENT trigger with batch size and a window up to 900 s.
Job runs nightly with no follow-up steps → Scheduler universal target `aws-sdk:glue:startJobRun`.

questions.q: The on-call team must get an email whenever any Glue job fails or times out. What is the lowest-effort solution?

options.t: A Lambda function that calls `GetJobRuns` every 5 minutes and emails failures
options.why: Wrong: polling code to build and run when Glue already emits events.

options.t: A CloudTrail trail with a rule matching `AWS API Call via CloudTrail` for `StartJobRun`
options.why: Wrong: that matches the start call, not the job outcome.

options.t: Enable Glue continuous logging and read the logs daily
options.why: Wrong: not an alert, and manual.

options.t: Rule on the default bus: `source=aws.glue`, `detail-type=Glue Job State Change`, `detail.state=["FAILED","TIMEOUT"]` → SNS topic with email subscription
options.why: Right: Glue publishes state-change events to the default bus for free, and SNS delivers email.

questions.explain: Glue Job State Change events + SNS is the standard failure alert.
questions.remember: Alert on an AWS service's state change → rule on the default bus matching its state-change event → SNS (email/chat). No polling code.
variants: Alert on Step Functions Standard failures → `Step Functions Execution Status Change` with FAILED/TIMED_OUT/ABORTED.
Express workflows emit no EventBridge events → use CloudWatch Logs/metrics.

questions.q: A platform team keeps its rules on a custom bus `ops-bus`. A rule there matching `aws.glue` events never fires, though Glue jobs fail often. What should they do?

options.t: Add a rule on the default bus that matches the Glue events and targets `ops-bus`
options.why: Right: AWS service events land only on the default bus; forward them to the custom bus.

options.t: Add a resource policy on `ops-bus` allowing `glue.amazonaws.com`
options.why: Wrong: Glue does not send to custom buses, whatever the policy says.

options.t: Change the rule state to `ENABLED_WITH_ALL_CLOUDTRAIL_MANAGEMENT_EVENTS`
options.why: Wrong: that is only for read-only CloudTrail events.

options.t: Turn on schema discovery on `ops-bus`
options.why: Wrong: discovery infers schemas; it does not route events.

questions.explain: Service events reach only the default bus.
questions.remember: AWS service events → default bus only. A rule on a custom bus never sees them unless a default-bus rule forwards them.
variants: S3 events wanted on a custom bus → same fix: forwarding rule on the default bus.
Events from other accounts wanted → cross-account bus target with a role plus receiver bus policy.

questions.q: A rule pattern is `{"source":["aws.glue"],"detail":{"state":["failed"]}}`. Failed jobs never trigger it. What is the fix?

options.t: Change `source` to `glue`
options.why: Wrong: AWS service sources start with `aws.`.

options.t: Wrap the pattern in `$or`
options.why: Wrong: `$or` gives OR across fields; it does not change case matching.

options.t: Use `"FAILED"` (or `equals-ignore-case`), because matching is case sensitive
options.why: Right: string matching is exact and case sensitive; Glue sends `FAILED`.

options.t: Use `{"exists": true}` on `state`
options.why: Wrong: that would match every state, including SUCCEEDED.

questions.explain: Pattern strings match exactly, case sensitive.
questions.remember: Rule never fires → test the pattern with `TestEventPattern`/Sandbox; check case, spelling, nesting and numbers-as-strings; use `equals-ignore-case` when case varies.
variants: Numbers 300 vs 300.0 do not match as plain values → use `numeric`.
A brand-new rule does not match a test sent at once → wait for propagation and retest.

questions.q: A producer calls `PutEvents` with 10 entries. The call returns HTTP 200, but only 7 events reach the targets. What should the producer do?

options.t: Nothing: HTTP 200 means all entries were accepted
options.why: Wrong: partial failures still return 200.

options.t: Check `FailedEntryCount` and retry only the entries that have an `ErrorCode`
options.why: Right: per-entry failures are reported in the response, not as an exception.

options.t: Retry the whole batch of 10
options.why: Wrong: resends 7 successful entries and creates duplicates.

options.t: Lower the batch to 1 entry per call
options.why: Wrong: costs more calls and does not handle failures.

questions.explain: PutEvents can partly fail with HTTP 200.
questions.remember: `PutEvents` 200 is not success for every entry → read `FailedEntryCount`, retry only failed entries with backoff. Throttling raises `ThrottlingException` → back off and retry.
variants: All events vanish with 200 and no failed entries → check the bus name; a missing bus silently drops events.
`ThrottlingException` → back off, batch up to 10 entries, or raise the quota.

questions.q: An application must publish an event that describes a 3 MB data file. What is the best design?

options.t: Split the file across several `PutEvents` entries
options.why: Wrong: consumers would have to reassemble pieces, and ordering is not guaranteed.

options.t: Request a quota increase for the event size
options.why: Wrong: the `PutEvents` request limit is 1 MB total.

options.t: Send the file through SNS instead
options.why: Wrong: SNS is not a large-payload transport either.

options.t: Store the file in S3 and put the object URL in the event (claim-check)
options.why: Right: events stay small and the 1 MB request limit is respected.

questions.explain: Large payloads go to S3; the event carries a pointer.
questions.remember: PutEvents = up to 10 entries and 1 MB per request; each 64 KB chunk is billed as one event. Big data → S3 + pointer.
variants: Producer sends 900 KB events and the bill is high → shrink them or use claim-check (each 64 KB chunk = one event).
Old practice exams say 256 KB → current notes say 1 MB per request.

questions.q: One rule must deliver every matching event to 7 different targets. What should the architect do?

options.t: Raise the targets-per-rule quota in Service Quotas
options.why: Wrong: 5 targets per rule is a fixed limit.

options.t: Split into two rules with the same pattern, or send to an SNS topic or another bus that fans out
options.why: Right: more rules, SNS or a bus target work around the fixed limit.

options.t: Use a Scheduler schedule with 7 targets
options.why: Wrong: a schedule has exactly one target.

options.t: Put all 7 targets in the rule's input transformer
options.why: Wrong: an input transformer shapes the payload; it does not add targets.

questions.explain: 5 targets per rule is a hard limit.
questions.remember: Need more than 5 targets → several rules with the same pattern, or fan out through SNS or another event bus.
variants: Thousands of subscribers or email/SMS → SNS fed by EventBridge.
Scheduler must reach 5 targets → point it at an event bus, SNS or Step Functions.

questions.q: A Lambda target was unavailable for 30 hours. The rule uses the default retry policy and has no DLQ. What happened to the events, and what prevents this next time?

options.t: They are kept in the bus until the target recovers; nothing to change
options.why: Wrong: EventBridge is not a queue; it does not store events for consumers.

options.t: They were retried for 24 hours and then dropped; add a standard SQS DLQ to the target
options.why: Right: default max event age is 24 hours; without a DLQ, exhausted events are lost.

options.t: They were sent to an SQS FIFO DLQ automatically
options.why: Wrong: there is no DLQ unless you set one, and FIFO queues cannot be DLQs.

options.t: They were retried for 7 days; raise the max age to 14 days
options.why: Wrong: `MaximumEventAgeInSeconds` max is 86,400 (24 hours).

questions.explain: Default retry = 185 attempts / 24 hours; then dropped unless a DLQ exists.
questions.remember: Classic rule targets retry up to 24 h and 185 attempts. Set a standard SQS DLQ (same Region) so exhausted events are kept; put SQS in front of fragile targets.
variants: DLQ creation fails with a FIFO queue → use a standard queue.
Events go to the DLQ at once with `NO_PERMISSIONS` → permission errors are not retried; fix the role or policy.

questions.q: A security team in `eu-west-1` created a rule to catch IAM `CreateUser` API calls via CloudTrail. A trail is active, but the rule never fires. Why?

options.t: IAM is a global service whose CloudTrail events appear only in us-east-1, so the rule must be there
options.why: Right: global service events are emitted only in us-east-1.

options.t: `CreateUser` is a read-only call and needs a special rule state
options.why: Wrong: `CreateUser` is a write call; write events match normal ENABLED rules.

options.t: CloudTrail events go only to custom buses
options.why: Wrong: they go to the default bus.

options.t: The rule must target an archive first
options.why: Wrong: archives store events; they do not affect matching.

questions.explain: Global service CloudTrail events appear only in us-east-1.
questions.remember: Rules on IAM or Route 53 API calls → create them in us-east-1 with an active trail. Read-only calls (Get/List/Describe) need `ENABLED_WITH_ALL_CLOUDTRAIL_MANAGEMENT_EVENTS`.
variants: Rule must react to `ListBuckets` → set state `ENABLED_WITH_ALL_CLOUDTRAIL_MANAGEMENT_EVENTS`.
Rule must react to S3 `GetObject` → that state plus S3 data events on the trail.

questions.q: A company uses an EventBridge global endpoint with event replication between two Regions. Which events are protected by its failover?

options.t: All events, including AWS service and partner events
options.why: Wrong: service and partner events are not covered.

options.t: Only AWS service events on the default bus
options.why: Wrong: these are exactly the ones not covered.

options.t: Only events written to an archive
options.why: Wrong: failover is not tied to archives.

options.t: Only custom events the application sends with `PutEvents`
options.why: Right: global endpoints cover custom events only.

questions.explain: Global endpoints fail over custom events only (about 6–7 minutes).
questions.remember: Keep producers sending during a Regional outage → global endpoint (Route 53 health check, same-named custom bus in both Regions, replication for automatic failback). Covers custom events only.
variants: Without event replication → failback must be done by manually setting the health check healthy.
Need to fail over AWS service events → not possible with global endpoints.

questions.q: An auditor asks why one custom event never reached its target. Metrics only show counts. Which feature gives a per-event record that proves whether any rule matched?

options.t: CloudTrail management events for the bus
options.why: Wrong: CloudTrail records API changes like `PutRule`, not per-event rule matching.

options.t: Schema discovery on the bus
options.why: Wrong: discovery infers event shapes, not delivery steps.

options.t: Event bus logging at INFO (or TRACE) level to CloudWatch Logs, Firehose or S3
options.why: Right: INFO logs ingested, rule matched, `No Rules Matched` and invocation results.

options.t: An archive with replay
options.why: Wrong: archives keep copies of events but do not say what matched.

questions.explain: Bus logging INFO records match / no match per event.
questions.remember: "Did my rule match?" → bus logging at INFO/TRACE (`No Rules Matched` proves a pattern problem). ERROR level logs only failures. Logs can include sensitive detail data.
variants: Pipes need the same visibility → Pipes logging (ERROR/INFO/TRACE).
Who changed a rule → CloudTrail `PutRule`/`PutTargets`.

questions.q: Messages arrive in an SQS queue and each must start a Step Functions workflow. The team wants no Lambda function and no custom polling code. What should they use?

options.t: An EventBridge rule with the SQS queue as event source
options.why: Wrong: rules do not poll SQS; queues are targets of rules, not sources.

options.t: An SNS subscription on the queue
options.why: Wrong: SQS cannot be subscribed to like a topic.

options.t: A Lambda event source mapping
options.why: Wrong: it can only invoke Lambda, which the team wants to avoid.

options.t: EventBridge Pipes with SQS as source and Step Functions as target
options.why: Right: Pipes poll the queue and invoke Step Functions directly.

questions.explain: SQS → Pipes → Step Functions, no Lambda.
questions.remember: Point-to-point "move records from a queue/stream to service X, maybe filter or enrich, no code" → EventBridge Pipes. Many-to-many routing → event bus rules.
variants: Source is S3, SNS or an event bus → not a Pipes source; use rules.
Need Lambda code anyway with ESM features → Lambda event source mapping.

questions.q: A pipe reads 10 million SQS messages a month but only messages with `type = ORDER_CREATED` matter to the target. How can the team cut cost the most?

options.t: Add a Pipes filter on `body.type`; only events that pass the filter are billed
options.why: Right: filtered-out events are free and never reach enrichment or the target.

options.t: Filter inside the enrichment Lambda
options.why: Wrong: every message is still billed as a pipe request and pays for Lambda.

options.t: Filter in the target Step Functions workflow
options.why: Wrong: pays for every pipe request and every execution.

options.t: Raise the SQS visibility timeout
options.why: Wrong: does not reduce the number of messages processed.

questions.explain: Pipes bill only events that pass the filter.
questions.remember: Filter as early as possible: Pipes filter before enrichment and target, rule patterns instead of Lambda filtering. Batching cuts Pipes requests further.
variants: Filter needs `wildcard` or `anything-but` with prefix → not supported on Pipes; only on buses.
Filtering on body content → the payload must be valid JSON.

questions.q: A pipe uses a Step Functions Standard workflow as its enrichment step. Soon after creation the pipe stops. Why, and what is the fix?

options.t: Enrichment must be synchronous; Standard workflows cannot run synchronously, so use an Express workflow
options.why: Right: only Express workflows (or Lambda, API Gateway, API destinations) can enrich.

options.t: The 5-minute execution limit was raised; request a higher limit
options.why: Wrong: the 5-minute pipe execution limit is fixed and not the cause.

options.t: The pipe role lacks `events:PutEvents`
options.why: Wrong: enrichment does not use PutEvents.

options.t: Standard workflows need an SNS topic in front
options.why: Wrong: no such requirement; they simply cannot be sync enrichments.

questions.explain: Pipes enrichment is always synchronous.
questions.remember: Pipes enrichment = Lambda, Step Functions Express, API Gateway or API destination, always REQUEST_RESPONSE. Standard workflows can only be async targets.
variants: Pipe auto-stopped → read `StateReason` first (usually IAM or networking).
Standard workflow as target → must be FIRE_AND_FORGET; Pipes cannot retry errors inside it.

questions.q: A pipe reads from Kinesis Data Streams and writes to an SQS queue. The engineer sets batch size 100 and the configuration is rejected. Why?

options.t: Kinesis sources allow at most 10 records per batch
options.why: Wrong: Kinesis can give up to 10,000 records.

options.t: The SQS target accepts at most 10 messages per batch, so the pipe max is 10
options.why: Right: batch size is limited by the smallest piece; SQS takes 10.

options.t: Pipes do not allow Kinesis as a source
options.why: Wrong: Kinesis Data Streams is a supported source.

options.t: Batching requires an enrichment step
options.why: Wrong: enrichment is optional.

questions.explain: Pipe batch size = the smallest limit across source and target.
questions.remember: Pipes batch limits by target: SQS/SNS/event bus 10, Kinesis and Firehose 500, CloudWatch Logs 10,000; Lambda/Step Functions limited by payload.
variants: Target is Firehose → up to 500.
Target is Lambda → it always gets a JSON array, even with batch size 1.

questions.q: A pipe reads from an Amazon MSK cluster in private subnets with no internet access and shows a connection error. What fixes it?

options.t: Make the MSK cluster publicly accessible
options.why: Wrong: not needed, and weakens security.

options.t: Add a dead-letter queue to the pipe
options.why: Wrong: Kafka sources have no DLQ support, and a DLQ would not fix connectivity.

options.t: Add a NAT gateway or a `pipes-data` VPC endpoint so Pipes can reach the cluster
options.why: Right: Kafka/MQ sources in a VPC need network access to Pipes.

options.t: Raise the pipe's concurrency
options.why: Wrong: concurrency does not create network paths.

questions.explain: Kafka/MQ sources in a VPC need NAT or a `pipes-data` endpoint.
questions.remember: Pipe in a VPC can't reach Kafka/MQ → NAT gateway or `pipes-data` VPC endpoint; MSK also needs security groups. Read `StateReason`.
variants: Poison record keeps failing on an MSK pipe → handle it in code; no DLQ for Kafka sources.
Pipe reading a CMK-encrypted SQS queue gets access denied → `kms:Decrypt` in key policy and role policy.

questions.q: A nightly job must start at 02:00 New York time all year, including across daylight saving changes. What is the best option?

options.t: A legacy scheduled rule with `cron(0 2 * * ? *)`
options.why: Wrong: scheduled rules are UTC only and ignore DST.

options.t: Two scheduled rules switched by hand at each DST change
options.why: Wrong: manual and error-prone.

options.t: A Glue crawler schedule
options.why: Wrong: does not start arbitrary jobs and is not the general answer.

options.t: EventBridge Scheduler cron schedule with time zone `America/New_York`
options.why: Right: Scheduler supports IANA time zones and handles DST.

questions.explain: Scheduler supports time zones; scheduled rules are UTC only.
questions.remember: New schedules → EventBridge Scheduler (time zones, one-time `at()`, flexible windows, millions of schedules, retries, DLQ). Scheduled rules are legacy, UTC only.
variants: Job must run once next Tuesday at 15:30 → Scheduler `at()` with `ActionAfterCompletion: DELETE`.
10,000 hourly schedules hit an API at the same second → flexible time window.

questions.q: A Glue job must start every night with no follow-up steps. The team wants the fewest moving parts. What should they create?

options.t: An EventBridge Scheduler schedule with universal target `aws-sdk:glue:startJobRun`
options.why: Right: universal targets call almost any API, so no Lambda or Step Functions is needed.

options.t: A scheduled rule with the Glue job as target
options.why: Wrong: Glue jobs are not classic rule targets.

options.t: Scheduler → Lambda → Glue `StartJobRun`
options.why: Wrong: works but adds code to maintain.

options.t: Scheduler universal target `aws-sdk:glue:getJobRuns`
options.why: Wrong: universal targets cannot call read-only actions, and it would not start the job.

questions.explain: Scheduler universal targets reach 6,000+ API actions.
questions.remember: Simple timed API call → Scheduler universal target. Multi-step work with retries/branches → Scheduler → Step Functions. Universal target input is not validated at create time: read the DLQ on failures.
variants: Schedule fails on every run but was created fine → bad universal target input; read DLQ `ERROR_MESSAGE`.
Need follow-up steps (crawler, notify) → Scheduler → Step Functions.

questions.q: A consumer bug corrupted 4 hours of output. The bus has an archive. Other rules on the bus must not process those events again. What should the team do after fixing the code?

options.t: Replay the 4-hour window to the same bus, limited to the affected rule
options.why: Right: replay can target specific rules on the source bus.

options.t: Replay the window to a new bus in another account
options.why: Wrong: replay goes back to the same source bus only.

options.t: Replay to all rules and rely on ordering
options.why: Wrong: other consumers get duplicates, and replay order is not the original order.

options.t: Restore the archive to S3 and reprocess manually
options.why: Wrong: archives are not exported this way; replay is the built-in path.

questions.explain: Replay → same bus, optionally to specific rules; events carry `replay-name`.
questions.remember: Archive + replay: replay a time window to the same bus, optionally to chosen rules; replays are time-sliced and unordered; targets must be idempotent or check `replay-name`. Max 10 concurrent replays.
variants: Events from 30 minutes ago needed → wait about 10 minutes after the window ends; archive delivery lags.
Replay by position with strict order → Kinesis Data Streams, not EventBridge.

questions.q: A rule must push Glue failure events to a SaaS incident tool's HTTPS API that uses OAuth client credentials. The team wants no Lambda. What should they use?

options.t: A Lambda function URL that forwards to the SaaS
options.why: Wrong: function URLs receive inbound webhooks; it adds code.

options.t: An API destination with a connection of type OAuth client credentials
options.why: Right: EventBridge stores the credentials in Secrets Manager and fetches and refreshes the token.

options.t: An SNS HTTPS subscription with the client secret in the URL
options.why: Wrong: leaks the secret and does not handle OAuth tokens.

options.t: A partner event bus for the SaaS
options.why: Wrong: partner buses receive events from SaaS; they do not send to it.

questions.explain: API destinations + connections call HTTPS APIs with Basic, API key or OAuth auth.
questions.remember: Outbound to SaaS/HTTP → API destination with a connection (secret kept in Secrets Manager; OAuth token refreshed for you). Inbound from SaaS → partner bus.
variants: Connection shows `DEAUTHORIZED` → update the credentials or OAuth settings.
Must drop sensitive fields before sending → input transformer on the target.

questions.q: An API destination calls a partner API that sometimes takes 8 seconds and sometimes returns HTTP 400 for bad input. Which statement is correct?

options.t: Both cases are retried for 24 hours
options.why: Wrong: 400 is not retried.

options.t: The 8-second calls succeed; 400 responses are retried with backoff
options.why: Wrong: the request timeout is 5 seconds, and 400 is not retried.

options.t: Calls time out after 5 seconds (and are retried); 400 responses are not retried, so add a DLQ and fix the input
options.why: Right: timeout 5 s max; retries only on 401, 407, 409, 429 and 5xx.

options.t: Raise the API destination timeout to 30 seconds
options.why: Wrong: 5 seconds is a fixed limit.

questions.explain: API destinations: 5 s timeout, retry only 401/407/409/429/5xx.
questions.remember: Slow API (> 5 s) → put a queue or async endpoint in front. Non-retried 4xx → DLQ and fix the transformer. Rate limit (default 300/s) delays, then drops events past 24 h.
variants: Endpoint returns 429 → retried, and `Retry-After` is honoured.
Rate limit far below event rate → backlog grows; add a DLQ or raise the rate.

questions.q: Every account in an AWS Organization must send Glue failure events to a central bus in the ops account. Which TWO items are required? (Choose 2.)

options.t: An IAM role on each sender rule that allows `events:PutEvents` on the central bus
options.why: Right: new cross-account bus targets need a role on the sender's rule.

options.t: A bus policy listing every account ID one by one
options.why: Wrong: works but is not needed; the org condition is simpler and fits the size limit.

options.t: An archive in every sender account
options.why: Wrong: archives are for replay, not routing.

options.t: A central bus policy with `Principal "*"` and condition `aws:PrincipalOrgID`
options.why: Right: grants the whole organization in one statement.

questions.explain: Cross-account bus routing = sender rule role + receiver bus policy.
questions.remember: Cross-account checklist: receiver bus policy (org condition), IAM role on the sender rule, receiver rule (with `account` in the pattern), receiver target permissions.
variants: Account B forwards A's events to C → C never gets them (third-account hop blocked).
Team only wants events in their SQS queue → direct cross-account SQS target with role and queue policy.

questions.q: About 200 small files land in S3 every minute. Each should not start its own Glue run; one run should process a batch. What is the best design?

options.t: A rule per file prefix starting a Glue job each
options.why: Wrong: still one run per file, and Glue jobs are not direct targets.

options.t: Scheduler every second
options.why: Wrong: not event-driven and wasteful.

options.t: S3 Event Notifications to Lambda that calls `StartJobRun`
options.why: Wrong: one run per file.

options.t: S3 → EventBridge rule → Glue workflow with an EVENT trigger using batch size and a batch window (up to 900 s)
options.why: Right: the trigger collects events and starts one run per batch.

questions.explain: Glue workflow EVENT trigger batches events.
questions.remember: Many events, one run → Glue workflow EVENT trigger with `BatchSize` and `BatchWindow` (≤ 900 s). Rule target role needs `glue:notifyEvent`.
variants: Multi-step ETL with retries and branches → EventBridge triggers Step Functions.
Glue workflow not starting → check `glue:notifyEvent` on the role and that S3 EventBridge is on.

questions.q: A compliance team requires a customer managed KMS key on a custom bus, and the data team also wants schema discovery on that bus. What is the outcome?

options.t: Discovery works once the key policy allows `schemas.amazonaws.com`
options.why: Wrong: discovery is not supported on CMK buses at all.

options.t: Discovery is not supported on a CMK bus; use a separate AWS-owned-key bus for discovery
options.why: Right: schema discovery cannot run on a bus encrypted with a customer managed key.

options.t: The CMK also encrypts AWS service events on the bus, so discovery is skipped only for those
options.why: Wrong: the bus CMK never covers AWS service events, and discovery is blocked entirely.

options.t: Switch to the Glue Schema Registry, which reads the bus
options.why: Wrong: the Glue Schema Registry is for Kafka/Kinesis serialization, not bus discovery.

questions.explain: Schema discovery and a bus CMK cannot be combined.
questions.remember: CMK bus: set a DLQ (key errors like `EVENT_DECRYPTION_FAILURE` go there), allow `events.amazonaws.com` in the key policy; no schema discovery; AWS service events still use an AWS owned key.
variants: CMK bus suddenly stops delivering → check if the key was disabled or its policy changed.
Encrypted SQS/SNS target → its key policy must allow EventBridge `kms:GenerateDataKey` and `kms:Decrypt`.

questions.q: A rule's `TriggeredRules` metric rises, but the Lambda target is never invoked. The function's resource policy for `events.amazonaws.com` includes a `SourceAccount` condition. What should be done?

options.t: Remove the `SourceAccount` condition and keep `SourceArn` set to the rule ARN
options.why: Right: the docs say a `SourceAccount` field can block EventBridge invocation.

options.t: Remove all conditions so any rule can invoke it
options.why: Wrong: opens a confused-deputy risk.

options.t: Add a DLQ to the Lambda function
options.why: Wrong: the event never reaches Lambda; the problem is the policy.

options.t: Raise the invocation quota
options.why: Wrong: throttling delays invocations; it does not block them.

questions.explain: Lambda permission with `SourceAccount` can block EventBridge.
questions.remember: Debug order: `MatchedEvents` → `TriggeredRules` → `Invocations` → `FailedInvocations`/DLQ. Rule triggered but target silent → permissions: resource policy scoped by `aws:SourceArn`, or an execution role.
variants: `Invocations` > 0 but nothing happens in Lambda → the function failed after async invoke; check its logs and async destinations.
Encrypted SQS target gets nothing → key policy must allow EventBridge.

questions.q: A security review finds that a developer added an extra target to a production rule and copied all matched events to a personal account. What is the best preventive control?

options.t: Encrypt the bus with a customer managed key
options.why: Wrong: EventBridge still decrypts and delivers to any configured target.

options.t: Turn on schema discovery
options.why: Wrong: unrelated to access control.

options.t: Restrict `events:PutTargets` (and `events:PutRule`) in IAM and alert on CloudTrail `PutTargets` events
options.why: Right: adding targets can exfiltrate every matched event, so treat it like data write access.

options.t: Lower the rule's retry attempts to 0
options.why: Wrong: does not stop a new target from receiving events.

questions.explain: `PutTargets` is effectively data access.
questions.remember: Least privilege: separate roles for producers (PutEvents on one bus ARN), rule admins (PutRule/PutTargets) and readers; audit rule changes with CloudTrail.
variants: Auditor asks who changed a rule → CloudTrail `PutRule`/`PutTargets`.
Bus accepts events from any account (`Principal "*"`, no condition) → add an org condition and `account` in patterns.

questions.q: A producer sends 900 KB custom events and the EventBridge bill is much higher than expected for the event count. Why?

options.t: Rule evaluation is billed per rule per event
options.why: Wrong: rule evaluation is not billed on classic buses.

options.t: Same-account target deliveries are billed per target
options.why: Wrong: custom events to same-account targets have no extra charge.

options.t: Custom events are billed per GB of storage
options.why: Wrong: classic buses bill per million events, not storage.

options.t: Each 64 KB chunk of an event is billed as one event, so a 900 KB event counts as many events
options.why: Right: billing is per 64 KB chunk; shrink payloads or use claim-check.

questions.explain: Classic bus billing: each 64 KB chunk = one event.
questions.remember: Classic cost: AWS service events free to ingest; custom/partner $1 per million; cross-account delivery $1 per million (sender pays); 64 KB chunks. Keep events small, filter in patterns, avoid loops.
variants: Rule fires forever and the bill spikes → infinite loop; narrow the pattern and add a Budgets alarm.
Scheduler cost → 14 million invocations free per month, then $1 per million.

questions.q: Which CloudWatch alarm tells the team that EventBridge is actively losing events because failed deliveries cannot even reach the DLQ?

options.t: `InvocationsFailedToBeSentToDlq >= 1`
options.why: Right: those events failed delivery and could not be stored in the DLQ, so they are lost.

options.t: `MatchedEvents = 0`
options.why: Wrong: only says nothing matched.

options.t: `ThrottledRules > 0`
options.why: Wrong: throttled invocations are delayed, not dropped.

options.t: `InvocationsSentToDlq >= 1`
options.why: Wrong: those events are safe in the DLQ for redrive.

questions.explain: DLQ delivery failure = data loss.
questions.remember: Alarm on `FailedInvocations >= 1` and `InvocationsFailedToBeSentToDlq >= 1`. Common DLQ faults: missing queue policy, wrong Region, FIFO queue, unusable KMS key. Many metrics appear only when non-zero.
variants: `FailedInvocations` alarm shows no data → normal when there are no failures.
Target delayed and `ThrottledRules` rising → raise quotas or buffer with SQS.
